title: Building an assessment
lede: How JABSOM actually does it: copy last year, then edit. Starting fresh is rare.

blocks.title: Start from last year's exam
blocks.text: With about nine years of items on the system, most JABSOM assessments get built by copying the previous year's exam and editing it. That keeps question order, categorization, and scoring setup intact, along with the institutional memory of what worked.
Copy and repost are different things

blocks.caption: Two ways to reuse an assessment
rows: Can set new password and dates
A make-up sitting or a missed cohort

blocks.title: For a new academic year, duplicate
blocks.text: A repost folds this year's results into last year's reports, which ruins year-over-year comparison. Duplicating gives the new exam its own Exam ID and its own reporting.

items.d: Name it with the academic year so the next person can find it.
Anything the course no longer teaches, plus items that performed badly in last year's analysis.
Write them in the bank first, then add them. Every new question needs at least one category.
Confirm point values, and that partial credit settings survived the copy.
Mind the 200 MB ceiling. See [Attachments and media](#attachments).
7 business days before the exam. Do not post it yourself unless OME asked you to.
